bullet_feedback.bullet: Precomputed popular workflows from a 270K+ row PostgreSQL table into a Redis-cached category tree to keep lookups within the database's permission and rate limits, which became the Claude skill's main search tool
bullet_feedback.problem: Four technical nouns ('PostgreSQL table', 'Redis-cached category tree', 'permission and rate limits', 'Claude skill') are chained before the reader learns what a 'workflow' is or who searches it; the payoff ('became the main search tool') is an internal-architecture outcome a recruiter can't weigh.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: A non-engineer cannot restate this bullet, so it adds nothing in the screen and reads as noise next to the stronger 65% bullet above it.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what a 'workflow' is in this product and who was searching for it; what 'permission and rate limits' were being protected
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Lead with the problem in plain words (the AI tool needed to search 270K+ workflows without overloading a rate-limited database), then the approach (precompute popular ones into a cached tree). Consider merging into the first Capital One bullet since it describes the search tool that bullet relies on.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Built an EventBridge-scheduled LLM-as-judge check for a production Amazon Bedrock classifier that rates research documents by importance to trigger fine-tuning only when its grades shift past a threshold
bullet_feedback.problem: 'EventBridge-scheduled LLM-as-judge check' front-loads two jargon terms; the sentence also doesn't say why retraining only on drift matters (cost? stability?), so the result is unclear.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: This is the only bullet about a production system on the contract, but a recruiter can't tell what was built or what it saved, so 'production' gets lost.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what the check protects against or saves by only retraining past a threshold
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Put the purpose first in plain words (a scheduled check that watches a production document classifier and only triggers retraining when its quality drifts), then name EventBridge/Bedrock after. 'LLM-as-judge' can stay but should come after the plain description.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Implemented B+ tree and LSM-tree backends for the engine's event log to compare them on identical 2M-record workloads, which showed the B+ tree giving 12.8x the read throughput and 22x faster range queries for 27% more disk
bullet_feedback.problem: The bullet reports a benchmark finding (12.8x, 22x, 27%) but not why the comparison was done or what decision it led to; 'backends', 'range queries' and the two tree names are opaque to a screener.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: For infra roles this is a strong storage-engine signal, but a recruiter can only pass it along as 'big numbers I don't understand', and three stacked metrics in one line blur which one matters.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what the comparison was used to decide (e.g., which store the engine kept)
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Add a short plain-language frame up front ('built two storage designs for the engine's event log and benchmarked them...') and end on the decision or tradeoff rather than three ratios; keep the 12.8x and drop or demote one of the other figures.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Designed the book as std::list FIFOs per price level inside a std::map with an order-ID hash map to make cancels O(1), which sustained 1.26M events/sec end-to-end over the full replay
bullet_feedback.problem: 'std::list FIFOs per price level inside a std::map with an order-ID hash map' is a noun stack of C++ container names; the reader has to parse three data structures before reaching the one result (1.26M events/sec).
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: Fails the read-aloud and plain-language tests; a recruiter will skip straight to the bold number and lose the design choice that earned it.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: State the goal first ('made order cancels constant-time'), then the design in fewer container names, e.g. 'queued orders per price level and indexed them by order ID so cancels are O(1)', then the 1.26M events/sec result.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Cut AI workflow generation time 65% to under 15s by splitting a Claude skill into focused sub-skills that call Python search and validation tools instead of searching open-ended
bullet_feedback.problem: 'AI workflow generation' and 'Claude skill / sub-skills' don't tell the reader what was being generated or for whom; 'searching open-ended' is a compressed phrase nobody says aloud.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: This is the most visible bolded win on the page, so the recruiter repeats it, but can only say 'made an AI thing faster'.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what a generated workflow is and who uses it
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Name the user and output in a few plain words before the method; replace 'instead of searching open-ended' with what the old behavior was (e.g., 'instead of letting the model search freely').

bullet_feedback.bullet: Co-built a research tool that scores and aggregates topics to show Amazon Leo's public-policy staff what's popular, which runs in dev on AWS Fargate with GitHub Actions CI/CD and AWS CDK infrastructure-as-code ready for production
bullet_feedback.problem: The second half ('runs in dev on AWS Fargate with GitHub Actions CI/CD and AWS CDK infrastructure-as-code ready for production') is a tech list; 'ready for production' reads ambiguously - deployed or not?
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The bullet's honest 'dev' status is good, but the tool list crowds out what the candidate personally built and the reader may wonder if it ever shipped.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: which part the candidate owned (e.g., the infrastructure setup vs. the scoring logic)
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Say what the candidate's part was, then name only the tools that explain it (e.g., if they owned deployment, 'set up the CDK-defined Fargate deployment and CI/CD'); move the rest to Skills.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Rebuilt a legacy test-data workflow tool as a React and TypeScript Electron app with a visual React Flow editor and Jest-tested validation to make editing smoother, which 90% of 30+ surveyed developers preferred
bullet_feedback.problem: Five technology names (React, TypeScript, Electron, React Flow, Jest) in one bullet; 'make editing smoother' is vague. It's also front-end work on an infra-targeted page.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: Minor cost: it dilutes the infra story and reads as a stack list, though the 90% survey result is clear.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Trim to the one or two technologies that explain the change (desktop app with a visual editor) and leave the rest to Skills.

page_feedback.problem: The AWS internship - the page's strongest infra signal (EC2 capacity planning) - has no bolded anchor and no result, while the first bold on the page is '65%' on an AI-tool bullet at Capital One.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: In a 7-second skim the eye lands on the AI-workflow win, so the recruiter's takeaway is 'AI tooling person' rather than 'infra/platform engineer'.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Make the AWS bullet's plain-language purpose ('how much spare EC2 capacity Redshift keeps for patching') the visual anchor, e.g. by tightening it so the key phrase leads; avoid adding metrics that don't exist.

page_feedback.problem: 'UMD App Development Contracting (Client: Amazon Leo)' is unclear to a recruiter: it's not obvious whether this is Amazon employment, a student club, or a paid contract, or what Amazon Leo is.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: Recruiters may either discount it as a club or suspect brand-borrowing; either way three strong AWS bullets lose weight.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: clarify: what the contracting group is in a few words in the title line (e.g., student contracting firm) so the Amazon Leo client relationship reads honestly.

page_feedback.problem: The order-book project, the most technically impressive and most performance/systems-relevant item, is at the bottom and two of its three bullets are dense C++/data-structure jargon.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: Infra and systems HMs would hire on this, but a screener reaching it last and not understanding it may not pass it along.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Keep it, but make its bullets restatable in plain words (see bullet feedback); the first bullet already does this well and is a model for the other two.

page_feedback.problem: Several bullets end with a trailing 'which ...' clause carrying the result (Capital One bullets 2 and 3, all three IEX bullets), giving the page a repeated stitched-sentence rhythm.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: Mild machine-written feel and results arrive late in long sentences, slowing the skim.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Vary structure in a few bullets so the result or purpose leads instead of trailing after 'which'.
